title: PCDFusion: Proposal-Context-Detail Bayesian Rendering for Infrared-Visible Image Fusion
claim: Modalities are physically asymmetric and each fails differently, so fusion should be a local posterior-weighted rendering that recovers structure where baselines fail.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; motivation, failure comparison, then method diagram
description: Three panels separated by thin vertical lines. Panel (a), 'Physical Asymmetry', shows a spectrum bar for visible (0.4–0.7 µm) and thermal IR (8–14 µm). Below it are a street photo and its dark infrared image. Green check and red cross labels mark the strengths and weaknesses of each modality: rich texture but dependent on light, versus weak texture but dependent on temperature. Panel (b), 'Failure Cases', has two rows of street scenes in columns Input, TarDAL and Ours. Red boxes and zoomed insets mark regions. Red '× Missing Building' and '× Blurry Branches' captions contrast with green '√ Complete Building' and '√ Clearer Branches'. Panel (c), 'Posterior Rendering', is a small flow diagram. Visible and infrared inputs feed a cross-modal observation network and a physical cues block. Both feed a sigmoid posterior equation, which drives three dashed stages (Positive IR Proposal, Context Update, Detail Rendering) that produce the fused output.
caption: PCDFusion estimates posterior action weights from physical cues and cross-modal observations, recovering structures under visible failure while suppressing unreliable thermal responses.
abstract: Infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF) aims to combine visible and thermal infrared observations for human perception and downstream vision tasks. Visible and thermal infrared observations are physically complementary but unreliable in different ways. Existing deep IVIF methods mainly improve feature interaction and reconstruction, but often lack an explicit local rule for deciding when visible appearance should dominate and when thermal responses should contribute. To address this issue, we reformulate IVIF as local Bayesian posterior rendering, where fusion is controlled by posterior action weights rather than direct modality mixing. In this paper, we propose Proposal-Context-Detail Fusion (PCDFusion), a visible-anchored framework that implements this formulation through three rendering stages. PCDFusion preserves potentially useful thermal responses, updates exposure-degraded visible regions, and renders reliable band-limited infrared structures into the final luminance. Extensive experiments on public IVIF benchmarks show that PCDFusion improves fusion quality, target recovery, and downstream detection and segmentation performance under challenging illumination. The code is available at https://github.com/BIT-RuiLiu/PCDFusion.git.
